## The world's longest international border stretches nearly 8,891 km, crossing forests, lakes and Arctic terrain. Another massive frontier runs for about 7,599 km as the longest continuous land boundary, shaped by steppe and history.

The world’s longest international border between Canada and US stretches nearly 8,891 km, crossing forests, lakes and Arctic terrain. (Photo: Jason Redmond / AFP)

https://www.indiatoday.in/author/india-today-education-desk
New Delhi,UPDATED: Dec 2, 2025 19:18 IST

Ever wondered which international boundary is the longest?
The longest international land border in the world runs between Canada and the United States (US). Stretching over approximately 8,891 kilometres (5,525 miles), this border runs from the Atlantic to the Pacific, and from temperate forests to Arctic shores.
Just behind it lies the frontier between Kazakhstan and Russia, roughly 7,599 kilometres long, which holds the distinction of being the longest continuous land border anywhere on Earth.

### CANADA AND THE US: A BORDER THROUGH LAKES, FORESTS AND COASTS

 The Canada–US border is far from a straight line. Instead, it winds through a patchwork of forests, lakes, rivers, coastal waters and Arctic landscapes.
A significant portion of the boundary lies across waterways, including the Great Lakes, meaning the border shifts between land and water segments.
Because of this weaving geography, the border is technically non-continuous, yet when all segments (land and water) are combined, it becomes the longest border between any two nations.
It touches multiple Canadian provinces and US states across thousands of miles.

### KAZAKHSTAN–RUSSIA: THE UNBROKEN STEPPE LINE
By contrast, the Kazakhstan–Russia border runs as a single, uninterrupted land boundary over vast plains and steppe.
There are no major lakes or oceans splitting it. That makes it the longest continuous terrestrial border on the planet.
This border was originally drawn as an internal administrative line during the Soviet era, between the Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic and the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic.
When the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991, those boundaries turned into an international frontier.

Kazakhstan-Russia border (Photo: AFP)

### WHY THE DISTINCTION MATTERS
The difference between a non-continuous and a continuous border matters more than it seems. A water-woven border like Canada–US reflects diverse geography: lakes, rivers, coastline, forests. Meanwhile, a straight continuous land frontier like Kazakhstan–Russia offers simpler terrain, continuous land access and easier administration.
For trade, migration, surveillance or travel, continuous land borders can be more straightforward to manage. Non-continuous borders, however, involve water bodies, joint water-management treaties and environmental cooperation.

### MORE THAN LINES: CROSS-BORDER LIFE
Borders are not just lines on a map, they are zones of contact, commerce and shared life.
The Canada–US border has supported major cross-border trade, travel between communities, and co-management of the Great Lakes and shared waterways.
The Kazakhstan–Russia frontier carries stories of history, ethnic links, migration across the Eurasian steppe, and post-Soviet transitions. Its long unbroken stretch still sees movement of goods and people between two of the world’s largest countries by area.
In short, whether zig-zagging across lakes or stretching straight across plains, these borders are far more than political demarcations. They are the corridors of human history, commerce and geography.
